properties.statement:
SURFACED 2026-08-16 BY THE WIDENED DEGREE-ZERO RULE, on its first run over reflow2's own graph — a finding nothing could previously report.

SEVEN TemporalFacts carry a `subject_id` naming a node THAT DOES NOT EXIST, and two of the seven are plainly typos for a live node:
  fact:dev-storyflow-fleet-log-triaged-2026-08-16          -> prj:reflow2      (the Project is proj:reflow2)
  fact:defect-kit-manifest-drift-is-invisible-to-ci        -> cap:thin-install (the node is req:thin-install)
  fact:defect-append-only-volatility-exempts-a-structural-rewrite
  fact:defect-link-artifact-has-no-type-for-a-test-source
  fact:dev-storyflow-fleet-log-full-triage-6203-lines-2026-08-16
  fact:reflow2s-black-boxes-hold-no-functions-allocation-went-straight-to-the-modules
  fact:the-music-graph-feedback-file-is-four-sessions-and-its-first-batch-was-fixed-long-ago

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE. `subject_id` is a required INDEXED property, so a fact names its subject without an edge — which means a fact is reachable by index lookup and never by a graph walk. Nothing validated that the id resolves. `orphan_node` ran on Decision only; `disconnected_community` reports clusters of >=2 and a node joined to nothing is never a cluster. So the pointer could be wrong for as long as it liked.

WHAT IT COSTS: the observation is stranded. It cannot be found from the thing it is about, it never enters an impact analysis, and a reader searching the live node's history sees nothing.

NOT REPAIRED HERE, and deliberately so: correcting a `subject_id` is a judgement about what the fact was about, not a mechanical fix, and the two obvious typos are the only two anybody could assert without reading each statement. RELATED, UNANSWERED: whether the schema should validate that a pointer property resolves at WRITE time — which would have stopped all seven at the door — or whether that couples the schema layer to graph contents in a way this design does not want.
